key_insight: ContextFocus introduces a lightweight activation-steering technique that nudges LLM hidden states to prioritize externally retrieved context over memorized parametric knowledge, substantially improving faithfulness when the two conflict.
problem_solved: When external evidence (e.g., up-to-date retrieval) conflicts with a model's internal knowledge, LLMs often default to memorized facts and produce unfaithful outputs; this work reduces that failure mode without expensive retraining.
method: Apply small, targeted adjustments to intermediate activations at inference time to increase the influence of retrieved context signals and suppress conflicting memorized activations.
Operate as a modular, lightweight steering layer compatible with retrieval-augmented pipelines — no full-model finetuning required.
Tune steering parameters on held-out context-conflict cases to balance faithfulness and fluency while preserving overall model behavior.
impact: Practitioners can deploy retrieval-augmented LLMs that more reliably follow external evidence with minimal compute and infrastructure changes, reducing hallucinations and the need for costly model updates. This improves real-world safety and maintainability for systems that depend on up-to-date knowledge.

paper_title: ContextFocus: Activation Steering for Contextual Faithfulness in Large Language Models
paper_authors: Nikhil Anand, Shwetha Somasundaram, Anirudh Phukan, Apoorv Saxena, Koyel Mukherjee
